facts.summary: One Nation One Ration Card (ONORC) enables eligible NFSA beneficiaries to access their entitled food grains through portability when they move between participating States or Union Territories.
purpose: Help migrant beneficiaries access their eligible food-grain entitlements away from their home location.
Enable beneficiaries to use the PDS network at participating locations.
facts.portability: An eligible beneficiary can use ration portability at a participating Fair Price Shop outside the location where the ration card was originally issued, subject to the applicable system and entitlement.
facts.migrant_beneficiaries: ONORC is particularly useful for beneficiaries who move to another State or Union Territory for employment or other reasons.
facts.authentication: Beneficiary authentication may be performed through the electronic Point of Sale (ePoS) system and the authentication mechanism supported by the applicable PDS system.
facts.ration_card: Beneficiaries generally do not need to obtain a new ration card solely because they temporarily move to another participating location under the portability framework.
facts.fair_price_shop: Portability can allow eligible beneficiaries to obtain their entitled food grains from a participating Fair Price Shop at their current location.
facts.eligibility: Access to portability depends on the beneficiary being covered under the applicable NFSA/PDS framework and the relevant ONORC implementation.
facts.state_implementation: ONORC operates across participating States and Union Territories through integration of their PDS systems.
important_notes: ONORC portability does not mean that ration-card eligibility rules are identical across all States/UTs.
The beneficiary's applicable entitlement remains subject to the relevant PDS and NFSA rules.
Do not assume that every PDS service is portable merely because ONORC portability is available.
Authentication and transaction requirements depend on the applicable PDS system.

faqs.question: What is One Nation One Ration Card?
faqs.answer: ONORC enables eligible NFSA beneficiaries to access their entitled food grains through PDS portability when they move between participating States or Union Territories.

faqs.question: Can I use my ration card in another State?
faqs.answer: Eligible beneficiaries can use ration portability at participating locations in another State or Union Territory under the ONORC framework, subject to the applicable system and entitlement.

faqs.question: Do migrants need a new ration card?
faqs.answer: A beneficiary generally does not need a new ration card solely because they temporarily move to another participating location under the portability framework.

faqs.question: Where can I collect ration under ONORC?
faqs.answer: Eligible beneficiaries can access their entitled food grains through participating Fair Price Shops at their current location.

faqs.question: How is a beneficiary verified under ONORC?
faqs.answer: Beneficiary authentication may be performed through the ePoS system and the authentication mechanism supported by the applicable PDS system.

faqs.question: Is ONORC available for every PDS service?
faqs.answer: No. ONORC concerns portability of eligible food-grain entitlements. Other PDS services may follow separate State/UT procedures.
